content: Prior work has developed sparse attention mechanisms, including applications to NMT BIBREF19, BIBREF12, BIBREF20, BIBREF22, BIBREF34. BIBREF14 introduced the entmax function this work builds upon. In their work, there is a single attention mechanism which is controlled by a fixed $\alpha $. In contrast, this is the first work to allow such attention mappings to dynamically adapt their curvature and sparsity, by automatically adjusting the continuous $\alpha $ parameter. We also provide the first results using sparse attention in a Transformer model.
